verdicts.quote: “This is a command-line interface (CLI) for mermaid. It takes a mermaid definition file as input and generates an SVG/PNG/PDF file as output.”
verdicts.reason: The docs describe a local CLI and file-in/file-out usage with no credentials or remote auth.
Only local installation/usage (and a local Node.js API) are documented; there’s no credential signup, OAuth, or hosted endpoint.

verdicts.quote: “This is a command-line interface (CLI) … generates an SVG/PNG/PDF file as output.”
verdicts.reason: There is no hosted API surface; the tool is a local renderer/CLI.

verdicts.quote: “The Mermaid MCP Server enables AI assistants to create, validate, and render Mermaid diagrams… [and] every tool call requires authentication with a Mermaid account. Authenticate automatically via OAuth 2.1…”
verdicts.reason: The vendor offers an official MCP server (Mermaid MCP Server). While it’s separate from the CLI, it is an official Mermaid-provided MCP, so not “none.”
There’s no viable hosted API to integrate; it’s a local tool only, which blocks a multi-tenant, cloud agent integration without bundling/running the CLI locally (blocker: local_tool_only).
